nodes.label: agent-router skill
nodes.rationale: Marked disable-model-invocation: true so it fires only from the explicit CLAUDE.md rule rather than auto-triggering on its description, which would double the context load.

nodes.label: Request classification (type / complexity / criticality)
nodes.rationale: Three axes are scored before dispatch so that criticality (money, prod code) can force a mandatory work-verifier pass instead of being decided ad hoc.

nodes.label: TASK ASSIGNMENT brief template
nodes.rationale: Internal brief for the Agent() call; deliberately not shown to the user in full — only a one-line routing summary — to save tokens.

nodes.label: Routing red flags
nodes.rationale: Encodes past failures: routing validation to the code writer, splitting one task across agents without coordination, telling the user 'no such agent' instead of calling agent-factory, and calling agent-factory for a task an existing agent already covers.

nodes.label: Priority tiers (High / Medium / Low)
nodes.rationale: High is reserved for prod bugs and news-hook content whose window is hours-days; month-scale strategy is deliberately Low.

nodes.label: task-coordinator skill
nodes.rationale: Also disable-model-invocation: true — invoked only by agent-router for complex multi-step work, so simple requests do not pay its context cost.

nodes.label: Atomic subtask decomposition
nodes.rationale: Each subtask must have one goal, be executable by a single agent from the agent-router roster, and have explicit success criteria — mixing responsibilities ('find and code it') is treated as two tasks.

nodes.label: Task card (ЗАДАЧА ДЛЯ)
nodes.rationale: Fixed slots (context, goal, inputs, requirements, constraints, output format, success criteria, dependencies) so the receiving agent never needs a clarifying round-trip.

nodes.label: Pre-issue card quality gate
nodes.rationale: Five checks (clarity, completeness, non-contradiction, feasibility, measurability); a single failure blocks issuing the card. Vague requests get a clarifying question instead of a fabricated card.

nodes.label: graphify pipeline skill
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder into a persistent knowledge graph with an honest EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail; reference files are split out and loaded only on their flag so a default run never pays for them.

nodes.label: Existing-graph fast path
nodes.source_location: What You Must Do When Invoked
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json exists and the request is a natural-language codebase question, skip Steps 1-5 entirely and query the graph — rebuilding would burn tokens to re-derive what is already on disk.

nodes.label: No-API-key policy
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally with no LLM, so a code-only corpus needs no key at all. Only GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY are ever read; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are never read, and prompting for one is explicitly called a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Part A - structural AST extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free; run in parallel with semantic subagents because the two operate on disjoint file types, saving 5-15s on large corpora.

nodes.label: Part B - semantic extraction via parallel subagents
nodes.rationale: Must use subagent_type=general-purpose: Explore is read-only and cannot write chunk files, which silently drops extraction results. All Agent calls go in one message or they run sequentially.
nodes.norm_label: part b - semantic extraction via parallel subagents

nodes.label: Semantic extraction cache
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to the extraction prompt file (SPEC_PATH) so a prompt upgrade forces re-extraction while an unchanged prompt replays entries (#1939). Only document/paper/image go to cache — flattening code in made subagents re-read every source file (#1392).

nodes.label: graph.json shrink guard
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write a graph smaller than the existing one (#479), and GRAPH_REPORT.md plus the analysis sidecar are only written after a successful write so they never describe a graph graph.json does not contain (#1392).

nodes.label: Graph health check (Step 4.5)
nodes.rationale: Read-only gate that surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops — the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. Never aborts, but must be surfaced per the Honesty Rules.

nodes.label: Community labeling (Step 5)
nodes.rationale: Suggested questions are regenerated after labeling because community labels change how the questions are phrased.

nodes.label: Manifest stamping and semantic-hash clearing
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped, so a failed chunk is re-queued next --update instead of being marked done and losing its content forever (#2015); dispatched-but-unstamped files get their stale semantic_hash cleared (#1948).

nodes.label: graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never render >5000-node HTML unwarned — the audit trail is the product.

nodes.label: Python interpreter detection (.graphify_python)
nodes.rationale: uv tool / pipx / venv installs mean the system python3 often cannot import graphify, so the resolved executable path is persisted to disk and substituted into every later bash block.

nodes.label: Extraction subagent prompt
nodes.rationale: Loaded only when a chunk holds a doc, paper or image; a pure-code corpus never reads it. It doubles as the cache key for semantic extraction.

nodes.label: Node ID format rule
nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative path with every directory level kept, so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and the ID matches what the AST extractor generates; filename-only or immediate-parent-only IDs create orphan ghost-duplicate nodes. Chunk suffixes are forbidden so IDs are deterministic regardless of which chunk processes the entity.

nodes.label: Discrete confidence_score rubric
nodes.rationale: Five fixed values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replaced a continuous range because production showed a bimodal collapse — >50% of edges at 0.5 and >40% at 0.85+ — meaning models were reading the range as a binary. If nothing fits, mark AMBIGUOUS rather than going below 0.4.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file rule
nodes.rationale: Keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

nodes.label: semantically_similar_to edge rule
nodes.rationale: Captures concepts that solve the same problem with no structural link (no import, call or citation); restricted to genuinely non-obvious cross-cutting cases so the graph is not flooded with trivial similarity.

nodes.label: Hyperedge rule (3+ participants)
nodes.rationale: Only for group relationships that add information beyond the pairwise edges — capped at 3 per chunk.

nodes.label: Constrained query expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches by case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch returns 0 hits. The question is expanded against the graph's own extracted vocabulary, capped at 12 tokens, with invented tokens forbidden and an empty result reported honestly rather than faked.

nodes.label: BFS traversal mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode, depth 3 — answers 'what is X connected to' with broad context, nearest neighbours first.

nodes.label: DFS traversal mode
nodes.rationale: Depth-limited to 6 to avoid traversing the whole graph; used for 'how does X reach Y' chain tracing.

nodes.label: Inline NetworkX traversal fallback
nodes.rationale: Used when the graphify query CLI is unavailable; matches the same way the binary does and enforces a ~4-chars-per-token output budget.

nodes.label: save-result feedback loop
nodes.rationale: Answers are written back into the corpus with the expanded-token trace embedded, so the next --update extracts the Q&A and the expansion history as graph nodes.

nodes.label: Work memory / LESSONS.md
nodes.rationale: Outcomes (useful / dead_end / corrected) accumulate into preferred sources, known dead ends and prior corrections; graphify reflect --if-stale keeps it current cheaply with no LLM.

nodes.label: --update incremental re-extraction
nodes.rationale: Populates .graphify_detect.json with 'files' = changed subset and 'all_files' = full corpus so downstream steps that read it unconditionally see the right state.

nodes.label: Code-only change fast path
nodes.rationale: If every changed file has a code extension, semantic extraction is skipped entirely — no subagents, no LLM cost.

nodes.label: build_merge replace-on-re-extract
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction survives (#801); every source_file in the new chunks is dropped from the base before merge (#1344), and directed=IS_DIRECTED must be passed or a --directed --update silently rebuilds undirected and collapses reciprocal edges (#1392).

nodes.label: prune_sources deletion-only rule
nodes.rationale: Only genuinely deleted files may be pruned — adding changed files here would delete the freshly re-extracted content, since with root= the prune set relativizes to the same base as the merged nodes. Without root= nothing is pruned at all and stale nodes accumulate every update (#1361).

nodes.label: --cluster-only self-contained rerun
nodes.rationale: graphify cluster-only regenerates report, graph.json and graph.html by itself; re-running Steps 5-9 would hit FileNotFoundError because the prior build's cleanup already deleted the intermediates (#1392).

nodes.label: Whisper video/audio transcription
nodes.rationale: Video and audio cannot be read directly, so they are transcribed to text and then treated as doc files in Step 3. The JSON result is written from Python rather than a shell redirect because Whisper prints progress to stdout and would corrupt the file (#1392).

nodes.label: Self-composed Whisper domain prompt
nodes.rationale: The host agent writes the domain hint itself from existing god-node labels — no separate API call needed. A video-only corpus falls back to a generic punctuation prompt.

nodes.label: /graphify add URL ingestion
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects URL type (YouTube/video, Twitter oEmbed, arXiv, PDF, image, generic webpage) into ./raw, then runs --update to merge the new file into the existing graph.

nodes.label: --watch folder watcher
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; doc/paper/image changes only raise a needs_update flag because they require paid semantic re-extraction. A 3s debounce stops a wave of parallel agent writes from triggering one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: graphify clone (GitHub repos)
nodes.rationale: Clones into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> and reuses existing clones on repeat runs.

nodes.label: merge-graphs cross-repo merge
nodes.rationale: For monorepos the skill pipeline would clobber a single graphify-out/, so each subfolder is extracted via the CLI (which writes graphify-out/ inside the scanned path) and merged at the root. Every merged node carries a repo attribute for origin filtering.

nodes.label: Post-commit auto-rebuild hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of running a background process; re-runs AST on files from git diff HEAD~1 and appends to any pre-existing hook rather than replacing it. Doc/image changes are ignored and need a manual --update.

nodes.label: graphify claude install (CLAUDE.md integration)
nodes.rationale: Writes a ## graphify section into the local CLAUDE.md so future sessions check the graph before answering codebase questions without a manual /graphify.

nodes.label: Neo4j export / push
nodes.rationale: Uses MERGE so re-running never creates duplicates.

nodes.label: FalkorDB export / push
nodes.rationale: Statements are OpenCypher but FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one at a time with no bulk script import, so --falkordb-push is preferred over the portable cypher.txt artifact.

nodes.label: graphify MCP stdio server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live. Claude Desktop cannot run $(...) and its system python3 cannot import graphify under uv, so the absolute interpreter path must be hardcoded.

nodes.label: Agent-crawlable wiki export
nodes.rationale: Must run before Step 9 cleanup while .graphify_labels.json still exists.

nodes.label: Token-reduction benchmark
nodes.rationale: Only runs above 5,000 total words — for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: LLM Council skill
nodes.rationale: Adapted from Andrej Karpathy's LLM Council; instead of different models it uses sub-agents with different thinking lenses inside Claude. Reserved for decisions where being wrong is expensive — not for one-right-answer, creation or processing tasks.

nodes.label: The Contrarian
nodes.rationale: Not a pessimist — assumes a fatal flaw exists and hunts for it, asking the questions the user is avoiding.

nodes.label: The First Principles Thinker
nodes.rationale: Its highest-value output is often 'you're asking the wrong question entirely'.

nodes.label: The Expansionist
nodes.rationale: Deliberately ignores risk — that is the Contrarian's job — and only asks what happens if this works better than expected.

nodes.label: The Outsider
nodes.rationale: Described as the most underrated advisor: zero context means it catches the curse of knowledge — things obvious to the user and confusing to everyone else.

nodes.label: The Executor
nodes.rationale: Judges every idea by 'what do you do Monday morning?' — a brilliant idea with no first step gets called out.

nodes.label: Workspace context enrichment
nodes.rationale: Scans CLAUDE.md, memory/, referenced files and prior council transcripts (≤30 seconds) so advisors give specific grounded advice instead of generic takes, and so the same ground is not re-counciled.

nodes.label: Anonymized peer review round
nodes.rationale: The step that makes this more than 'ask 5 times' — Karpathy's core insight. Responses are relabeled A-E with randomized mapping so reviewers evaluate on merit instead of deferring to a favoured thinking style or position.

nodes.label: Chairman synthesis / COUNCIL VERDICT
nodes.rationale: Fixed five-part structure ending in one concrete next step; the chairman is explicitly allowed to side with a lone dissenter against 4 advisors when the reasoning is strongest, and must not smooth over genuine clashes.

nodes.label: Request routing rule (first contact via agent-router)
nodes.rationale: agent-router is invoked via Skill, not Agent — it is the model's own classification procedure, not a separate subagent. Both routing skills are disable-model-invocation so this written rule is their only trigger, avoiding a doubled context load. A trivial one-step request may go straight to an executor.
nodes.norm_label: request routing rule (first contact via agent-router)

nodes.label: research → build → verify pipeline
nodes.rationale: The standard conveyor shape for this repo's multi-agent work.

nodes.label: Agent roster (.claude/agents/)
nodes.rationale: Ported from the shared agent repo LecksLecks/Slom; trading agents irrelevant to this repo were deleted at the user's explicit request.

nodes.label: Single-writer Metricool restriction
nodes.rationale: smm-instagram-manager is the only agent with write access to the Metricool calendar and always sets draft: true with no exceptions; every other IG/Threads agent is read-only or hands finished material to it.

nodes.label: Mandatory token-economy section
nodes.rationale: Every agent file must carry this section; only the prose around the output is trimmed — the agent's mandatory output format is never cut.

nodes.label: instagram-agent-supervisor (roster entry)
nodes.rationale: Entry point for IG/Threads/n8n work: brief → dispatch → independent checklist verification → report.

nodes.label: work-verifier (roster entry)
nodes.rationale: Independent read-only audit with a PASS/FAIL verdict; kept separate from the code writer so validation is never done by the author.

nodes.label: agent-factory (roster entry)
nodes.rationale: Designs, writes, registers and immediately runs a new agent in the same turn — but must first check the roster for a near-duplicate, because this repo already paid the cost of overlapping agents once.

nodes.label: Love lecks month-1 growth plan
nodes.rationale: Target of 100k followers in 3-6 months is judged honestly unreachable (~2% at 3 months, ~8-12% at 6 months); the plan builds a system that maximizes the weekly chance of a viral hit rather than promising a date.

nodes.label: Reach-to-follow conversion gap
nodes.rationale: ≈508,000 cumulative cold reach produced under 3,000 followers (<0.5%) because people shared someone else's video rather than following the author — so conversion, not reach, is bottleneck #1. Month-1 target is 1.2-1.5%.

nodes.label: Meta aggregator algorithmic penalty
nodes.rationale: Policy effective 30.04.2026 against accounts aggregating others' content; visible in the data as median reach falling 1,240 → 490 (−60%), matching the documented penalty range. Moving to 100% original content is therefore a condition for lifting the penalty, not a taste preference — and a 2-4 week reduced-distribution tail is expected even on original content.

nodes.label: 68% view-rate cold-feed gate
nodes.rationale: The only metric with a proven link to reach: all 7 reels at ≥68% view rate reached the cold feed (600-183,000), 50-62% capped at 600-1,800, ≤45% was dead. Formats below 45% are not repeated and never go into the pinned set.

nodes.label: Content pillars
nodes.rationale: Reworked under the brand platform into flagship 'Стоп. Перемотай.' (50%), 'Я не понял, но кивнул' (20%), price/cat/new-format rotations (10% each). Justified by IGRE data: an acted scene beats a talking head 3-5× (#абсурд 3.46% ER vs 0.67-0.88% for car monologues).

nodes.label: Weekly format mix (100% reels)
nodes.rationale: Zero static/carousel in month 1 because average post reach is 8.8× lower than reel reach (649 vs 5,707); 25% of slots are reserved for experimenting with new formats.

nodes.label: «Стоп. Перемотай.» anchor ritual
nodes.rationale: A repeatable personality anchor chosen to fix the conversion bottleneck. Alternatives were rejected on evidence: 'Смена №___' puts a text plate in the first seconds and competes for attention, threatening the 68% gate; the cat 'Приёмка' is unmanageable at 3-5 videos/week and an end-of-video anchor cannot reach viewers who dropped off. The phrase and gesture must stay unchanged for 20+ videos to become recognizable.

nodes.label: Brand platform (approved 28.07.2026)
nodes.rationale: Answers one question — 'это ведь ненормально, или я один так думаю?' Masculine grammatical gender in every network without exception; a gender error counts as a defect.

nodes.label: Tone of voice rules
nodes.rationale: First-person masculine singular, spoken Russian with sparing profanity, statement not complaint, no position of superiority, and no moral at the end — the ritual closes the scene instead.

nodes.label: Anti-positioning (what the brand is not)
nodes.rationale: Excludes politics/war/tragedy, hustle-success content, follow-for-follow and giveaways, mentoring/therapy, sketch for its own sake, reaction videos, insider-only diary content (every scene must land from the cold feed), 18+ and humiliation of identifiable people.

nodes.label: Visual code standard
nodes.rationale: One wired earphone always visible, chest-height 9:16 framing, daylight with no ring light (gloss kills the genre), no LUT, real backgrounds, one-take with cuts only on the ritual and the ending, ≤5-word titles, 0.5-1s static face at the end.

nodes.label: Profile entry point (avatar, name, bio, pins)
nodes.rationale: Directly targets the conversion hole: avatar readable at 40×40 px with the earphone and cord visible, name 'Алешка • стоп, перемотай', three pins ordered 3→2→1, and a 30-day measurement window with no parallel changes so the effect is attributable. Bio variant B is held for an A/B test after 3 weeks.
nodes.norm_label: profile entry point (avatar, name, bio, pins)

nodes.label: Publication guardrails
nodes.rationale: Masculine gender checked before every draft; a format under 68% view rate is not scaled or pinned; the catchphrase is frozen for 20+ videos; anything hinting at income, health or before/after goes to ig-compliance-checker; facts about the author's life only with his confirmation.

nodes.label: Draft-only publication policy
nodes.rationale: Everything is staged as draft: true; going live is a deliberate owner decision in Metricool, and for Instagram each post needs explicit owner confirmation — the Threads exception does not extend to Instagram.

nodes.label: Pilot batch (3 scripts)
nodes.rationale: «Автомастер», «Шкаф в 33» and «Родительский чат» — all one-take, all carrying the ritual at 60-70% of runtime, shot in a single day with video 1 needing hard daylight.

nodes.label: Viral Reels batch #2 (K1-K6)
nodes.rationale: Full cycle trend-scan → concepts → shot-by-shot scripts → captions. Original audio only, since the account is under the aggregator penalty and cannot risk others' tracks.

nodes.label: Trend scan (27.07)
nodes.rationale: Netflix documentary confessional (3-5 day window), the 'Bangladesh' escalation structure (device only, not the track) and expectation/reality were adopted; JJK hand-sign (oversaturated), 'girl grip' (someone else's voice) and Coldplay kiss cam (someone else's private drama) were rejected.

nodes.label: K6 «Кто-то же должен сказать» (pinned manifesto)
nodes.rationale: Filmed as a scene rather than a car monologue and released only after 2-3 flagships, then pinned as slot ③.

nodes.label: K5 «Ты это тоже видишь?» field template
nodes.rationale: Reactive slot published within 24h of a find and given priority over any scheduled slot it collides with. Only genuinely found objects — nothing fabricated — with brands and bystanders' faces kept out of frame.
nodes.norm_label: k5 «ты это тоже видишь?» field template

nodes.label: Shoot schedule and publication slots
nodes.rationale: Batched by lighting and location (daylight outdoor first, indoor in the evening); evening Reels slots with the Metricool calendar verified empty through 05.09, and K2 timed to a Threads post the next morning.

nodes.label: Agent pipeline status table
nodes.rationale: Tracks the handoff chain: strategist/creative-director/producer/copywriter done; shooting is the user's step; editor, compliance check and Metricool drafting are still blocked on footage.
